title: Bokhara couching
subtitle: A self-couched filling where many small tying stitches form diagonal lines across the laid thread
excerpt: Bokhara couching is a self-couching filling stitch in which a single thread both lays the long filling stitch and ties it down in one continuous movement. Unlike Romanian couching, Bokhara couching makes many small, closely spaced tying stitches across each laid thread, producing a distinctive diagonal grid pattern on the surface. It is associated with Central Asian embroidery and gives a firm, closely worked fill.
sourceNotes: Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Bokhara couching entry. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), couching and laid work chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). The stitch is documented in connection with Central Asian (Uzbek / Bokhara) needlework traditions.

glossaryTerms.definition: A filling method where one thread both crosses the shape as the laid thread and returns to tie itself down, without a separate couching thread.

content.text: stitch from Central Asian embroidery tradition. The thread crosses the shape as a long laid stitch, then the same thread makes a series of short, tight tying stitches at regular intervals back across the laid thread before crossing the shape again for the next row. The repeated tying stitches build diagonal lines across the filled area, giving the surface its characteristic patterned texture.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 3 to 4 strands, or crewel wool; a single twisted thread shows the tying stitches most clearly

content.text: Bring the thread up at point (A) on the left edge of the shape. Carry it across to point (B) on the right edge and take it down. This is the first laid thread.

Bring the needle up at point (C), a short distance inside the right edge and just below the laid thread. Take the needle over the laid thread and back down at point (D), just above the laid thread and slightly to the left of (C). This makes the first small tying stitch, which lies at a slant across the laid thread.

Bring the needle up again a short step to the left, still close to the laid thread. Work a second tying stitch in the same way. Continue making small slanting tying stitches at even intervals across the laid thread until you reach the left edge.

At the left edge, bring the needle up at the left edge just below the previous row to begin the next laid thread. Carry the thread across to the right edge, take it down, and work the return row of tying stitches from right to left. Offset the tying stitches so they fall between those of the row above, building up the diagonal pattern.
Continue filling the shape row by row, keeping the tying stitches evenly spaced and the laid threads parallel. Fasten off securely at the back when the shape is filled.

items.symptom: The tying stitches look irregular and scattered
items.cause: Spacing between tying stitches varies from row to row.
items.fix: Mark the tying stitch positions lightly before starting, or count fabric threads to keep intervals consistent. Work all tying stitches with the same slant direction.

items.symptom: The laid threads show gaps or humps between tying stitches
items.cause: The tying stitches were placed too far apart or pulled too tight, drawing the laid thread up into ridges.
items.fix: Space tying stitches no more than 4 to 5 mm apart. The tying stitch should lie snug against the laid thread without pulling it out of line.

items.symptom: The diagonal pattern does not align across rows
items.cause: Tying stitches in each row were not offset from those in the row above.
items.fix: On alternate rows, start the first tying stitch at the halfway point between the first two tying stitches of the previous row. This offset builds the diagonal grid.
